title: Background stability: identification of the witness geometry across λ

key_results.statement: For two places $h\neq h'$, either $Z(h,h')=(0,\infty)$ or $Z(h,h')$ is discrete (possibly empty or infinite) and disjoint from $(0,\varepsilon_{hh'})$ for some $\varepsilon_{hh'}>0$.

$Z(h,h')=(0,\infty)$ iff $(K_h-K_{h'})K_h^{\,j}\lvert\chi\rangle=\mu_0K_h^{\,j}\lvert\chi\rangle$ for $j=0,\dots,d_c-1$, with $\mu_0=\langle K_h\rangle-\langle K_{h'}\rangle$; such pairs have $d_0(h,h')=0$.

Off the discrete set $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}:=\bigcup_{h\not\equiv h'}Z(h,h')$, which is disjoint from some $(0,\varepsilon)$, the partition is constant: $\mathcal P(\lambda)=\mathcal P_{\rm gen}:=H/{\equiv}$, where $h\equiv h'$ iff $Z(h,h')=(0,\infty)$.

For $\lambda\in\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$, $\mathcal P(\lambda)=\mathcal P_{\rm gen}/{\approx_\lambda}$ is strictly coarser than $\mathcal P_{\rm gen}$: generic points only merge there, exactly when $W(x,x';\lambda)=1$, and never split.

The finite family $\mathcal F=\{W(x,x';\cdot)\}\cup\{W(x,y;\cdot)-W(x,x';\cdot)\}$, over distinct $x,x',y\in\mathcal P_{\rm gen}$, whose signs determine $N_V$ off $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$ as a fixed Boolean function.

$N_V$ is constant on each component of $(0,\infty)\setminus(\Lambda_{\mathcal P}\cup Z_{\mathcal F})$, where $Z_{\mathcal F}$ is the union of the zero sets in $(0,\infty)$ of the members of $\mathcal F$ that do not vanish identically; hence $\Lambda_N\subseteq Z_{\mathcal F}\setminus\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$ is discrete, with no condition on the records beyond finite $d_c$ and $\lambda$-independent $K_h$.

$\lambda_*=\min(\Lambda_{\mathcal P}\cup\Lambda_N)\in(0,\infty]$, so $\lambda_*>0$ always ($\lambda_*=\infty$ iff the set is empty); on $(0,\lambda_*)$ the background is $(\mathcal P_{\rm gen},N_V^{(0)})$ with $N_V^{(0)}$ the small-$\lambda$ graph, which is the graph of (11.11) when its two assumptions hold.

For the body of 17, the trajectory $\lambda\mapsto(P_x(\lambda))_{x\in\mathcal P_{\rm gen}}$ with $P_x=\sum_{h\in x}p_h$ is defined for every $\lambda\notin\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$ (indeed on all of $(0,\infty)$) and is real-analytic; at points of $\Lambda_N$ the curve is unchanged and only the neighbour relation among the fixed points changes.

Trajectories on background intervals separated by points of $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$ join unconditionally through the identification by places; at $\lambda_0\in\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$ the trajectory lives on the coarser points $X$ with $P_X(\lambda_0)=\sum_{x\subseteq X}\lim_{\lambda\to\lambda_0^{\pm}}P_x(\lambda)$.
Qubit line ($K_{h_i}=i\sigma_x$, $n\ge3$): $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}=\{\pi p/q:\ p\ge1,\ 1\le q\le n-1,\ \gcd(p,q)=1\}$, and $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}\cap(0,\pi]$ consists of those with $p\le q$.

Qubit line at $\lambda=\pi p/q\in\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$: the points are the $q$ residue classes mod $q$, giving one point for $q=1$, two points with $W=0$ and no edge for $q=2$, and for $q\ge3$ the cycle $N_V=C_q$ with $[i]\sim[i\pm\bar p]$, $p\bar p\equiv1\bmod q$.

Qubit line: $\lambda_*(n)=\pi/(\lfloor3n/2\rfloor-1)$, i.e. $2\pi/(3(n-1))$ for odd $n$ and $2\pi/(3n-2)$ for even $n$, with $\pi/(2(n-1))<\lambda_*<\pi/(n-1)=\min\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$ and $\lambda_*\notin\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$.

Qubit line, $\lambda\in(0,\pi)\setminus\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$: all places are separate points, and $N_V$ is the path $h_1-\dots-h_n$ for $\lambda\in(0,\lambda_*)\cup(\pi-\lambda_*,\pi)$ and the cycle $\mathcal C(\lambda)$ of cyclically adjacent $z_i=i\lambda\bmod\pi$ for $\lambda\in[\lambda_*,\pi-\lambda_*]$.
Qubit line: $\Lambda_N\cap(0,\pi]=\{\lambda_*,\pi-\lambda_*\}$ with $\lambda_*(n)$ from (24.18), and $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$ and $\Lambda_N$ are $\pi$-periodic on $(0,\infty)$.

Qubit line, on $(0,\lambda_*)$: $\delta(\lambda)=0$ for $\lambda\le\pi/(2(n-1))$ and $\delta(\lambda)=2-\pi/((n-1)\lambda)$ for $\pi/(2(n-1))\le\lambda<\lambda_*$; $\sup\delta$ is $1/2$ for odd $n$ and $(n-2)/(2(n-1))$ for even $n$, not attained.

Line with $K_{h_i}=iX$, $\sigma_X>0$: with $\Sigma_\chi$ the set of eigenvalues $\mu$ of $X$ of positive weight $w_\mu$ in $\chi$, $F(s)=\bigl\lvert\sum_{\mu\in\Sigma_\chi}w_\mu e^{-is\mu}\bigr\rvert^2$ and $F(s)=1$ iff $s(\mu-\mu')\in2\pi\mathbb Z$ for all $\mu,\mu'\in\Sigma_\chi$.

Line with $K_{h_i}=iX$: if the differences $\mu-\mu'$ ($\mu,\mu'\in\Sigma_\chi$) are commensurable and generate $g\mathbb Z$, then $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}=\{Tp/q:\ p\ge1,\ 1\le q\le n-1,\ \gcd(p,q)=1\}$ with $T=2\pi/g$, and $\mathcal P(Tp/q)$ consists of the residue classes mod $q$; otherwise $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}=\emptyset$.

Line with $K_{h_i}=iX$ ($\sigma_X>0$, $n\ge3$): $s_m/(n-1)\le\lambda_*\le s_c/(n-1)$, where $s_m$ ends the first strictly decreasing stretch of $F$ and $s_c$ is the least $s>0$ with $F(s)\ge F(v)$ for all $v\in[s/2,s]$; hence $\lambda_*=\Theta(1/n)$ and $\lambda_*\in\Lambda_N$, and in the commensurable case $\lambda_*<\min\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$.

Line with $K_{h_i}=iX$, on $(0,\lambda_*)$: $\delta(\lambda)=\max_{1\le k\le n-1}\bigl\lvert A(k\lambda)/(\sigma_Xk\lambda)-1\bigr\rvert\le\rho_F((n-1)\lambda)\le\rho_F(s_c)$, with $A(s)=\arccos\sqrt{F(s)}$ and $\rho_F(s)=\sup_{0<u\le s}\bigl\lvert A(u)/(\sigma_Xu)-1\bigr\rvert=O(s^2)$, a bound uniform in $n$.

Window medium ($m\ge2$, $n\ge2m$), for every $\lambda>0$: at $\lambda\in\pi\mathbb Z_{>0}$ all places form one point; at $\lambda\in\pi/2+\pi\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ the points are singletons with no edges; otherwise the points are singletons and $h_i\sim h_j$ iff $\lvert i-j\rvert=1$ or $\lvert i-j\rvert\ge2m-1$.
Window medium: $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}=\pi\mathbb Z_{>0}$, $\Lambda_N=\pi/2+\pi\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and $\lambda_*=\pi/2$ for all $n\ge2m$, $m\ge2$, independent of $n$.

Window medium, on $(0,\lambda_*)=(0,\pi/2)$: $\delta(\lambda)=\max_{1\le k\le m}\bigl[1-\arccos(\cos^{2k}\lambda)/(\sqrt{2k}\,\lambda)\bigr]\in(0,1)$, with $\delta=(2m-1)\lambda^2/12+O(\lambda^4)$ as $\lambda\to0$ and $\delta\to1-1/\sqrt{2m}$ as $\lambda\to\pi/2$. The maximum is attained at $k=m$ for every $\lambda\in(0,\pi/2)$, so $\delta(\lambda)=1-\arccos(\cos^{2m}\lambda)/(\sqrt{2m}\,\lambda)$.

Line with $K_{h_i}=iX$, off $\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$: the edge indicator is $e_{ij}(\lambda)=1$ iff $F(k\lambda)>0$ and no $l\notin\{i,j\}$ has $\min(F(\lvert i-l\rvert\lambda),F(\lvert l-j\rvert\lambda))>F(k\lambda)$, with $k=\lvert i-j\rvert$; and $\lambda_0\in\Lambda_N$ iff $\lambda_0\in Z_b\setminus\Lambda_{\mathcal P}$ and $e(\lambda_0^-)$, $e(\lambda_0)$, $e(\lambda_0^+)$ are not all equal, where $Z_b=Z_{\mathcal F}$ is the discrete set of $\lambda$ with $F(k\lambda)=F(k'\lambda)$ for some $1\le k<k'\le n-1$ or $F(k\lambda)=0$ for some $1\le k\le n-1$.

Spectral support of X in χ

open_issues: (b): Λ_N is characterized exactly by (24.30), but only implicitly. The candidates Z_b are roots of F(kλ)=F(k′λ) and F(kλ)=0, which have no closed form for general X. s_m, s_c, τ are defined from F but are not in closed form in general.

consistency_checks.check: λ → 0: in the qubit line α/λ = |i−j| = d₀ exactly for λ ≤ π/(2(n−1)), matching (5.10) and (5.15) (δ = 0); N_V is the path, which is (11.11) for d₀ = |i−j|, and its assumptions hold since max(|i−l|, |l−j|) ≠ |i−j|; in the window medium δ → 0.

Periodicity and mirror symmetry: Λ_P of (24.13) (p/q → (q−p)/q) and Λ_N = {λ_*, π−λ_*} are invariant under λ → π−λ, as (24.14) requires; in the window medium πℤ and π/2+πℤ are invariant under λ → π−λ and λ → λ+π.

Direct evaluation: for n = 3 at λ = π/3, α(h₁,h₂) = α(h₂,h₃) = α(h₁,h₃) = π/3, so by the tie rule the graph is a triangle, while for π/4 < λ < π/3 the point h₂ blocks (h₁,h₃) since λ < π−2λ, hence λ_*(3) = π/3 as in (24.18); for n = 4 at λ = π/5, α(h₁,h₄) = 2π/5 = max(α(h₁,h₂), α(h₂,h₄)) so the tie keeps the edge, while below π/5, 2λ < π−3λ blocks it, hence λ_*(4) = π/5.

response_to_verification.where: Step 8.2, Λ_N in general (new exact rule (24.30)); Result 3(b) and Open issues updated
